metadata.response_storage: Responses remain in the reviewer's browser until exported.

assumptions.title: New protected on-road infrastructure
assumptions.source: Infrastructure Victoria / Trafficworks Priority Cycling Corridor Investment Analysis (July 2025)
assumptions.explanation: Applied to missing, unverified and partial facilities. Major intersections, bridges, crossings and lighting are excluded from the kilometre rate.
assumptions.observed_effect: For the fixed 100 km portfolio, BCR is 0.72 under P50 and 1.79 under the low-complexity cost bound.
assumptions.review_question: Are these kilometre rates and exclusions credible for Melbourne SCC delivery, and where would site complexity materially change them?

assumptions.title: Conversion of a painted or inadequate facility to protected
assumptions.basis: Published central/low benchmark; high is a derived +30% case
assumptions.source: Infrastructure Victoria / Trafficworks; high upgrade value derived in this study
assumptions.explanation: The low case represents uncomplicated protected retrofit or road-space reallocation, not a painted-lane treatment.
assumptions.observed_effect: Lower upgrade cost causes early portfolios to be dominated by conversions of existing painted or inadequate corridors.
assumptions.review_question: Which mapped upgrade candidates could genuinely be protected at the low, P50 or high rate?

assumptions.title: Maintenance, renewal and asset lives
assumptions.basis: Published O&M/lives plus conservative modelled renewal
assumptions.source: Victorian cost study for O&M and lives; renewal treatment is a study assumption
assumptions.explanation: The appraisal uses like-for-like full-cost renewal, residual value at year 30, and a 10% program-management allowance.
assumptions.observed_effect: Removing renewal entirely raises the fixed-network BCR only from 0.72 to 0.84.
assumptions.review_question: Are the asset lives, annual maintenance, renewal fraction and program-management allowance consistent with agency experience?

assumptions.title: Existing, upgrade and missing SCC classification
assumptions.current_value: missing or unverified 59.5%; protected existing 26.9%; upgrade candidate 13.6%
assumptions.basis: Spatial reconciliation of SCC chainage and MATSim/OSM-derived facility attributes
assumptions.source: 2020 Strategic Cycling Corridors, MATSim network attributes and SCC reconciliation audit
assumptions.explanation: Protected status takes precedence over upgrade and missing representations at the same SCC chainage. Parallel-link conflicts are constrained to avoid duplicate investment.
assumptions.observed_effect: Status reconciliation reduced the candidate pool and removed redundant selections; remaining classifications have not been checked against a complete as-built inventory.
assumptions.review_question: Do these shares and mapped statuses resemble the current network, and which corridors are already protected, committed or misclassified?

assumptions.title: Definition of a completed intervention
assumptions.current_value: Every selected project becomes protected or off-road infrastructure
assumptions.source: Protected-cycling intervention definition used throughout the optimisation
assumptions.explanation: A painted or inadequate lane selected for investment is treated as conversion to separation; missing links receive new protected infrastructure.
assumptions.observed_effect: This prevents a favourable low cost from being interpreted as delivery of another painted lane.
assumptions.review_question: Is protection the appropriate minimum treatment, and are there corridors where another treatment should be considered?

assumptions.title: Level-of-traffic-stress classification
assumptions.current_value: Link LTS derived from speed, road type, lanes, traffic and facility attributes
assumptions.basis: Transferred published rules implemented in the companion cycling-safety code
assumptions.source: Pemberton/Jafari LTS calculation applied to the MATSim network
assumptions.explanation: Candidate exposure is the high-stress length encountered on the reconstructed bicycle route.
assumptions.observed_effect: Project benefits depend directly on which links are classified LTS 3 or 4 before treatment.
assumptions.review_question: Are the mapped stress classifications plausible, particularly on arterials, shared paths and low-speed streets?

assumptions.title: Maximum substitutable car-trip distance
assumptions.explanation: Only simulated car trips at or below this threshold can divert to cycling.
assumptions.observed_effect: The threshold defines the eligible trip population before any project is evaluated.
assumptions.review_question: Is 12 km a reasonable metropolitan screening threshold, and should e-bike and conventional-bike markets be separated?

assumptions.title: Response to reduced high-stress exposure
assumptions.source: Melbourne VISTA multinomial mode-choice model; independent estimate of -0.754 used as a cross-check
assumptions.explanation: The coefficient is applied as a binary pivot conditional on an observed simulated car trip, rather than as a newly estimated intervention model.
assumptions.observed_effect: Uncertainty in this coefficient is propagated through the scenario draws and risk-adjusted portfolio objective.
assumptions.review_question: Does the implied uptake appear credible for protected-corridor interventions, and what local before-after evidence should be used to calibrate it?

assumptions.title: Program-wide uptake uncertainty
assumptions.explanation: The same scenario-level uptake multiplier affects all trips in a draw, representing common uncertainty in realised adoption.
assumptions.observed_effect: The best-found preferred program changes from $21.4M at lambda 0 to $9.2M at lambda 0.25 and $5.6M at lambda 0.5.
assumptions.review_question: Is this range of program-wide uptake uncertainty credible, and are there important corridor-specific uncertainties missing?

assumptions.title: Bicycle-route impedance
assumptions.current_value: Bendigo route-choice coefficients; protected 0.716, painted 1.221, low-speed 0.942, steep slope -0.477 per km
assumptions.source: Bendigo PSL route-choice model (PPGIS, n = 258 routes), companion manuscript
assumptions.explanation: Coefficients estimated from 258 mapped routes of current cyclists in Greater Bendigo are converted to link impedances for Melbourne route reconstruction.
assumptions.observed_effect: Alternative routing specifications retain 78–100% of the central selected project set, while program length and benefit vary more.
assumptions.review_question: Are these route preferences transferable to prospective Melbourne cyclists, and which route conditions are missing?

assumptions.title: Appraisal period and discount rate
assumptions.current_value: 30 years; 7% real discount rate; sensitivities 4% and 10%
assumptions.explanation: Benefits, maintenance, renewal and residual value are discounted over the same appraisal period.
assumptions.observed_effect: Discount-rate sensitivities are reported separately rather than used to tune the central BCR.
assumptions.review_question: Is this appraisal frame appropriate for current Victorian cycling investment decisions?

assumptions.title: Health, safety, decongestion and vehicle-cost values
assumptions.current_value: Health system $0.72/km; private health $1.48/km; safety $1.31/km x 40% risk reduction x treated share; decongestion $0.60/km; VOC $0.18/km
assumptions.source: Australian Transport Assessment and Planning active-travel guidance
assumptions.explanation: Private health and safety use the rule of half; safety is additionally weighted by the trip's actual treated route share.
assumptions.observed_effect: Health and decongestion account for most monetised benefit; emission damage remains a relatively small component.
assumptions.review_question: Are these values and their application consistent with current agency appraisal practice?

assumptions.title: Expansion from the simulation sample
assumptions.current_value: 10% population sample expanded x10; modelled day annualised by 230 days
assumptions.source: AToM baseline design and appraisal configuration
assumptions.explanation: Trip outcomes from the calibrated 10% AToM run are expanded to metropolitan annual totals.
assumptions.observed_effect: The multiplier scales all trip-based benefits and physical emission changes.
assumptions.review_question: Are the sample expansion and 230-day annualisation appropriate for commuting and non-commuting cycling benefits?

assumptions.title: Downside-risk preference
assumptions.basis: Study decision preference, not an estimated behavioural parameter
assumptions.explanation: The objective blends expected benefit with the mean of the weakest 10% of uptake scenarios, then subtracts certain delivery cost in preferred-scale mode.
assumptions.observed_effect: Risk-neutral: $21.4M, 26.1 km, BCR 1.33; central: $9.2M, 10.9 km, BCR 1.69; lambda 0.5: $5.6M, 7.3 km, BCR 2.00.
assumptions.review_question: How should weak-uptake outcomes influence program size, and is lambda 0.25 a useful decision case?

assumptions.title: Funding ceiling versus spending target
assumptions.current_value: Two reported views: use available funding, or find the risk-adjusted preferred scale
assumptions.explanation: The full-funding view identifies the strongest portfolio under each ceiling; preferred-scale mode may leave funds unspent.
assumptions.observed_effect: Under P50 costs and lambda 0.25, the best-found preferred program spends about $9.16M; larger full-funding portfolios continue to add benefits but eventually reduce net value.
assumptions.review_question: In practice, should the cycling allocation be treated as fixed, contestable, or an upper ceiling that can be returned or redirected?

assumptions.title: Benefits not represented
assumptions.current_value: Existing cyclists, new/generated trips, shifts from public transport or walking, safety-in-numbers, equity and land-use accessibility are outside the quantified objective
assumptions.explanation: The response model counts existing car trips that switch when their potential bicycle route becomes less stressful.
assumptions.observed_effect: Omitted benefits may particularly affect larger connected networks, but no unmeasured uplift is added to the BCR.
assumptions.review_question: Which omitted outcomes are material enough to change project priorities, and what defensible data could quantify them?

assumptions.title: Fixed origins and destinations
assumptions.current_value: Current AToM trip origins, destinations and activity locations are held fixed
assumptions.source: AToM baseline replay and one-shot infrastructure response
assumptions.explanation: The model improves route quality for the current pattern of activities; it does not create nearby destinations or represent long-run land-use change.
assumptions.observed_effect: This may limit cycling uptake where otherwise rideable areas lack accessible everyday destinations.
assumptions.review_question: Where should cycling infrastructure be considered jointly with activity centres, schools, stations or other destination planning?
